words.enDefinition: A student who investigates a question and advises a partner organisation as part of a project.

examples.en: Each student consultant spent a morning at the food cooperative before suggesting any changes.
examples.zh: 每位「学生咨询顾问」都在食品合作社待了一个上午，才提出调整建议。

examples.en: A student consultant explained how our volunteer records had helped the team understand what delayed deliveries.
examples.zh: 一名「学生咨询顾问」解释了志愿者的记录怎样帮团队了解送货拖延的原因。

collocations: assign a student consultant to a project

words.enDefinition: A course in which students learn consulting by working on a real problem with an organisation.

examples.en: I took a consulting practicum that paired our class with a local bicycle repair charity.
examples.zh: 我选了一门「咨询实践课」，我们班和当地一家自行车维修慈善机构对接。

examples.en: The consulting practicum met on Fridays so client teams could join discussions before the weekend.
examples.zh: 「咨询实践课」安排在周五，这样合作单位的团队可以在周末前参加讨论。

words.enDefinition: A defined period of work in which consultants help a client address an agreed problem.

examples.en: Our consulting engagement focused on how the community theatre scheduled its rehearsal rooms after school.
examples.zh: 我们的「咨询项目合作」关注社区剧院怎样安排放学后的排练室。

examples.en: The student team completed a consulting engagement with a museum that wanted shorter booking queues.
examples.zh: 学生团队和一家希望缩短预约队列的博物馆完成了「一次咨询项目合作」。

words.enDefinition: An organisation that brings a problem to a student team and works with it on the project.

examples.en: Our client partner showed us how volunteers registered deliveries at the local food cooperative.
examples.zh: 「提出委托的合作机构」向我们演示了当地食品合作社的志愿者怎样登记送来的货物。

examples.en: We asked the client partner whether weekend bookings were recorded separately from weekday reservations.
examples.zh: 我们问「提出委托的合作机构」，周末的预约是否与工作日的预约分开记录。

words.enDefinition: A person who passes questions, information, and updates between the client and the project team.

examples.en: The client liaison confirmed which members of staff we could interview about the booking process.
examples.zh: 「客户联络人」确认了我们可以采访哪些员工来了解预约流程。

examples.en: Our studio named a client liaison to collect questions from both sides before each meeting.
examples.zh: 我们工作室指定了一名「客户联络人」，在每次会议前收集双方的问题。

words.enDefinition: A senior person in an organisation who backs a project and helps it get attention and resources.

examples.en: The executive sponsor introduced us to the people who ran the museum's group booking service.
examples.zh: 「项目的高层支持者」把我们介绍给负责博物馆团体预约服务的人。

examples.en: Our executive sponsor attended the midpoint review and asked the department to share anonymised totals.
examples.zh: 我们的「项目高层支持者」参加了中期评审，请该部门共享匿名化的汇总数据。

words.enDefinition: The person on the client's side who coordinates its part of the work with the student team.

examples.en: The client-side lead booked time with volunteers so we could observe their afternoon intake routine.
examples.zh: 「客户方项目负责人」和志愿者约了时间，让我们观察他们下午接收物品的流程。

examples.en: Our client-side lead checked the figures before sharing the findings with the museum director.
examples.zh: 「客户方项目负责人」先核对了数字，再把调查发现发给博物馆馆长。

words.enDefinition: The process of assigning projects to teams according to factors such as skill, interests, and availability.

examples.en: The course coordinator finished project team matching before putting students in touch with their clients.
examples.zh: 课程协调员完成「项目与团队匹配」后，让学生与各自的客户取得联系。

examples.en: Project team matching took longer when several groups asked to study the same museum service.
examples.zh: 几个小组都想研究博物馆的同一项服务，「项目与团队匹配」耗时更久。

words.enDefinition: A meeting at the start of a project at which the team and client discuss what they will do together.

examples.en: We held the client kickoff at the bicycle workshop to see where repairs were booked.
examples.zh: 我们在自行车维修工场开了「与客户召开的启动会」，现场看看维修预约在哪里办。

examples.en: At the client kickoff we agreed to start by reviewing the last month's booking totals.
examples.zh: 在「与客户召开的启动会」上，我们商定先核对上月的预约总量。

words.enDefinition: A list of topics to discuss at the first meeting of a project.

examples.en: We shared the kickoff agenda with the theatre manager before visiting the rehearsal rooms on Monday.
examples.zh: 周一去看排练室之前，我们把「启动会议程」发给了剧院经理。

examples.en: The kickoff agenda included time to confirm what the cooperative hoped to learn about volunteer scheduling.
examples.zh: 「启动会议程」安排了时间，确认合作社想从志愿者排班方面了解什么。

collocations: add an item to the kickoff agenda

words.enDefinition: A document recording a project's purpose, roles, boundaries, and how the team plans to work.

examples.en: The project charter named the student coordinator and explained when the client would review progress.
examples.zh: 「项目章程」列明了学生协调员，并说明客户会在什么时候审查进度。

examples.en: We revised the project charter after learning that only two branches could join the study.
examples.zh: 得知只有两个分点能参与这项研究后，我们修改了「项目章程」。

words.enDefinition: A clear description of what a particular project is intended to achieve.

examples.en: Our main project objective was to reduce the number of unanswered booking requests at the theatre.
examples.zh: 我们的主要「项目目标」是减少剧院未获回复的预约申请。

examples.en: The client asked whether interviewing both teams would help us achieve the project objective.
examples.zh: 客户问，采访两个团队能否帮助我们实现「项目目标」。

collocations: check work against a project objective

words.enDefinition: A problem an organisation wants to understand or address as part of its operations.

examples.en: The food cooperative described its business challenge as getting enough volunteers during busy collection hours.
examples.zh: 食品合作社提出了一个「经营难题」，就是怎样在领取高峰时招到足够的志愿者。

examples.en: Our client explained the business challenge before we discussed possible sources of information with staff.
examples.zh: 客户先说明「经营难题」，我们随后和员工讨论可从哪里获取资料。

words.enDefinition: A short document or explanation from the client describing the problem and what it wants the team to do.

examples.en: The client brief explained why the museum wanted to understand delays in school group bookings.
examples.zh: 「客户项目说明」解释了博物馆为什么想查清学校团体预约拖延的原因。

examples.en: We read the client brief before asking the cooperative which changes it had already tried.
examples.zh: 我们先阅读了「客户项目说明」，再问合作社已经尝试过哪些调整。

words.enDefinition: The person who leads and coordinates the consulting team's work with a particular client.

examples.en: The engagement lead assigned someone to count bookings and someone else to arrange the visit.
examples.zh: 「咨询项目牵头人」安排一人统计预约，另一人协调参观。

examples.en: Each engagement lead reported to the instructor after the first client meeting of the term.
examples.zh: 学期的第一次客户会议结束后，每位「咨询项目牵头人」都向老师作了汇报。

collocations: ask the engagement lead to coordinate

words.enDefinition: A person inside an organisation who actively builds support for a proposed project or change.

examples.en: The museum's education coordinator became an internal champion for simplifying the school group booking process.
examples.zh: 博物馆的教育协调员成了「组织内部推动者」，支持简化学校团体预约流程。

examples.en: We asked an internal champion to explain the proposed change at the client team's weekly meeting.
examples.zh: 我们请一位「组织内部推动者」在客户团队的周会上说明拟议改动。

words.enDefinition: The person you speak with about ordinary questions or scheduling at the partner organisation.

examples.en: Sara was our day-to-day contact at the gallery while we reviewed its visitor booking process.
examples.zh: 我们审查画廊访客预约流程期间，萨拉是我们在画廊的「日常联络人」。

examples.en: We sent small scheduling questions to our day-to-day contact instead of waiting for the review meeting.
examples.zh: 遇到小的日程问题，我们发给「日常联络人」，不用等到评审会再问。

words.enDefinition: A plan setting out the tasks, timing, and assigned responsibilities for a project.

examples.en: The project work plan placed staff interviews before the review of weekend booking patterns.
examples.zh: 「项目工作计划」把员工访谈安排在分析周末预约规律之前。

examples.en: We updated the project work plan after the cooperative offered access to a second collection site.
examples.zh: 合作社同意让我们去第二个领取点之后，我们更新了「项目工作计划」。

collocations: review a project work plan with the client

words.enDefinition: The person coordinating one defined area of work within a larger project.

examples.en: The workstream lead for field research organised visits to compare the two museum entrances.
examples.zh: 实地调研的「分项工作负责人」安排了参访，比较博物馆的两个入口。

examples.en: Each workstream lead reported one finding and one question for the rest of the group.
examples.zh: 每位「分项工作负责人」报告了一项发现，并给小组其他成员提了一个问题。

collocations: ask the workstream lead to report

words.enDefinition: The regular pattern of meetings, updates, or reviews that keeps project work moving.

examples.en: We agreed on a project cadence with short calls during weeks when the theatre was busy.
examples.zh: 我们商定了「项目沟通与推进节奏」，剧院忙的那几周只做简短通话。

examples.en: The project cadence changed when the client asked to review findings every other Friday.
examples.zh: 客户提出每隔一周的周五看一次调查发现，「项目沟通与推进节奏」也就调整了。

words.enDefinition: A group that reviews a project's direction and helps decide what should happen next.

examples.en: The steering group asked which branch could try the new booking form with fewer disruptions.
examples.zh: 「项目指导小组」问，在哪个分点试用新预约表影响会更小。

examples.en: We briefed the steering group after the theatre and museum teams compared their attendance figures.
examples.zh: 剧院组和博物馆组对比到场人数后，我们向「项目指导小组」作了汇报。

words.enDefinition: The authority different people or groups have to make particular project decisions.

examples.en: The project charter clarified decision rights for changing the questions we planned to ask volunteers.
examples.zh: 项目章程明确了有哪些人有权改志愿者访谈问题，也就是这方面的「决策权限」。

examples.en: We discussed decision rights after two managers gave different advice about testing the new form.
examples.zh: 两位经理对测试新表格给出不同意见后，我们讨论了「决策权限」。

collocations: record decision rights in the charter

words.enDefinition: Indicators used to judge whether a project has achieved the intended result.

examples.en: We chose success measures that the repair shop could follow without collecting extra customer details.
examples.zh: 我们挑了几项「衡量项目成效的指标」，维修店不用多收客户信息就能跟踪。

examples.en: One of our success measures was how long customers waited before getting a booking confirmation.
examples.zh: 客户等预约确认需要多久，是我们的「衡量项目成效的指标」之一。

words.enDefinition: A diagram of the people and groups affected by a project or able to influence it.

examples.en: Our stakeholder map included volunteers who ran the desk and visitors who made group bookings.
examples.zh: 我们的「利益相关方关系图」包括在服务台值班的志愿者和办理团体预约的访客。

examples.en: The faculty adviser checked our stakeholder map and asked who else could approve a trial.
examples.zh: 指导老师看了我们的「利益相关方关系图」，并问还有谁能批准试行。

collocations: show relationships on a stakeholder map

words.enDefinition: Arrangements that put the project team in touch with people affected by or influential in the work.

examples.en: The client arranged stakeholder introductions before we visited the two community centres on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五我们到两个社区中心走访前，客户安排了「利益相关方引荐」。

examples.en: We asked for stakeholder introductions so we could hear from both volunteers and bookers.
examples.zh: 我们请求安排「利益相关方引荐」，以便听听志愿者和预约者两方的看法。

words.enDefinition: A call held each week so the team and client can discuss the project's progress.

examples.en: We brought an example of a delayed booking to the weekly client call on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 周二的「每周客户通话」上，我们举了一个预约拖延的例子。

examples.en: The weekly client call gave the theatre manager a chance to ask about our initial findings.
examples.zh: 「每周客户通话」给了剧院经理一个机会，可以问问我们有哪些初步发现。

collocations: prepare for a weekly client call
bring a question to the weekly client call

words.enDefinition: Ideas accepted for planning or analysis until the team can check whether they are true.

examples.en: Our working assumptions included the idea that each centre recorded cancellations in the same way.
examples.zh: 我们的「工作中的暂定假设」之一，是各中心用同一种方式记录取消预约。

examples.en: We revisited our working assumptions after the charity gave us attendance data for two more months.
examples.zh: 慈善机构多给了两个月的到场数据后，我们重新审视了「工作中的暂定假设」。

words.enDefinition: To check that the people doing the work will be able to see or use the information they need.

examples.en: We needed to confirm access to data before planning which booking patterns to compare.
examples.zh: 我们需要先「确认可以获取数据」，再计划比较哪些预约规律。

examples.en: The project lead asked us to confirm access to data with the museum's research office.
examples.zh: 项目负责人让我们和博物馆研究办公室「确认可以获取数据」。

collocations: confirm access to data with the client
ask someone to confirm access to data
confirm access to data before analysis

words.enDefinition: To request documents or other information that explain the setting and history of a project.

examples.en: We took time to ask for background material about how the cooperative had grown recently.
examples.zh: 我们专门「索要了背景资料」，想了解合作社近期是怎么发展起来的。

examples.en: The student team chose to ask for background material before interviewing the theatre's front desk staff.
examples.zh: 学生团队决定先「索要背景资料」，再采访剧院前台工作人员。

collocations: ask for background material before a visit
ask for background material about the service
ask for background material at kickoff

words.enDefinition: To share a document or other material for people to read before a meeting.

examples.en: We agreed to send a pre-read showing the two booking processes before the review meeting.
examples.zh: 我们商定在评审会前「发送会前预读材料」，展示两种预约流程。

examples.en: Could you send a pre-read to the museum manager so she can check the terminology?
examples.zh: 你能给博物馆经理「发送会前预读材料」吗？这样她可以核对术语。

collocations: send a pre-read before the review
send a pre-read to the client
ask someone to send a pre-read

words.enDefinition: A task, event, or input that another part of the project needs before it can proceed.

examples.en: Access to the booking records was a project dependency for comparing the two locations fairly.
examples.zh: 要公平比较两个地点，拿到预约记录是一个「项目依赖条件」。

examples.en: The client agreed to help with one project dependency by introducing us to the volunteer coordinator.
examples.zh: 客户同意帮忙落实一个「项目依赖条件」，把我们介绍给志愿者协调员。

words.enDefinition: The early stage of a project in which the team learns about the organisation and the problem.

examples.en: During the discovery phase we read the charity's guides and learned how it allocated appointments.
examples.zh: 「初步了解阶段」，我们读了慈善机构的指南，了解了他们怎样分配预约。

examples.en: The discovery phase took longer because both theatre sites had different ways of recording cancellations.
examples.zh: 两个剧院场点记录取消预约的方式不同，「初步了解阶段」因此花了更长时间。

words.enDefinition: The period when a team analyses evidence to explain what is causing the problem.

examples.en: The diagnostic phase showed that most missed appointments came from a gap in the reminder process.
examples.zh: 「问题诊断阶段」发现，大多数爽约是预约提醒流程有缺漏造成的。

examples.en: We used the diagnostic phase to determine why theatre requests were answered faster at one site.
examples.zh: 我们在「问题诊断阶段」查明，为什么剧院有一个场点处理申请更快。

collocations: conduct interviews during the diagnostic phase

words.enDefinition: A planned conversation with someone affected by the project or able to inform its decisions.

examples.en: A stakeholder interview with a volunteer coordinator helped us understand how spare shifts were assigned.
examples.zh: 我们与志愿者协调员做了一次「利益相关方访谈」，了解了临时空班的分配方式。

examples.en: We changed the questions for our next stakeholder interview after visiting the museum entrance.
examples.zh: 走访博物馆入口后，我们改了下一场「利益相关方访谈」的问题。

words.enDefinition: An interviewee's agreement to take part or to allow a particular use of the interview.

examples.en: The student team recorded interview consent before taking notes on how volunteers greeted new visitors.
examples.zh: 学生团队先记录「受访者同意」，才记下志愿者怎样接待新访客。

examples.en: Our adviser checked that we had interview consent before we quoted anyone in the draft.
examples.zh: 在草稿中引用受访者的话之前，指导老师先核对我们是否已取得「受访者同意」。

words.enDefinition: A visit made specifically to see how an activity or process is carried out in practice.

examples.en: We arranged an observation visit to see how the repair charity recorded appointments during opening hours.
examples.zh: 我们安排了「现场走访观察」，了解维修慈善机构在开放时段怎样登记预约。

examples.en: The observation visit showed us how many people arrived without a confirmed time that afternoon.
examples.zh: 「现场走访观察」让我们看到，当天下午有多少人没确认预约时间就来了。

collocations: take notes during an observation visit

words.enDefinition: A guided walk through a location to see where work happens and how areas or steps connect.

examples.en: A site walkthrough helped us understand why some customers never saw the collection signs.
examples.zh: 一次「现场走查」让我们明白，有些客户为什么始终没看到取货指示。

examples.en: We completed the site walkthrough before asking about the second entrance on the floor plan.
examples.zh: 我们完成「现场走查」后，才问平面图上的第二个入口。

collocations: take notes during the site walkthrough

words.enDefinition: To watch a staff member at work for a period in order to understand their routine.

examples.en: We asked to shadow a staff member while they handled repair appointments at the front desk.
examples.zh: 我们请求「跟随一名员工观察工作」，看对方怎么在前台处理维修预约。

examples.en: A student consultant went to shadow a staff member on the museum's busiest weekday.
examples.zh: 博物馆一周中最忙的工作日，一名学生咨询顾问去了现场「跟随员工观察工作」。

collocations: arrange to shadow a staff member
shadow a staff member for an hour
ask to shadow a staff member

words.enDefinition: A list of documents, figures, or other information the team asks the client to provide.

examples.en: We sent an information request list before asking staff to compare their two booking forms.
examples.zh: 请员工比较两个预约表之前，我们发了一份「所需资料清单」。

examples.en: The client reviewed our information request list and offered totals for all four visitor entrances.
examples.zh: 客户看了我们的「所需资料清单」，愿意提供全部四个访客入口的汇总数据。

words.enDefinition: A request to obtain particular data needed for a project.

examples.en: The project data request asked for daily counts of visitors without including anyone's contact details.
examples.zh: 「项目数据申请」要求提供每天的访客人数，无须提供任何人的联系方式。

examples.en: Our client lead clarified the project data request before sending it to the records team.
examples.zh: 客户方负责人把「项目数据申请」说明清楚后，发给了记录管理团队。

collocations: follow up on a project data request

words.enDefinition: Data supplied by a client for the team to use in its project work.

examples.en: We checked the dates in the client data before comparing weekdays with weekend group bookings.
examples.zh: 我们先核对「客户提供的数据」里的日期，再对比工作日和周末的团体预约。

examples.en: The client data covered only the main venue, so we asked for the second location's totals.
examples.zh: 「客户提供的数据」只涵盖主场馆，所以我们索取了第二个场点的汇总数据。

collocations: check the quality of client data

words.enDefinition: To combine information from several interviews to find shared themes and important differences.

examples.en: Our team met to synthesise interviews with volunteers from both locations in the booking study.
examples.zh: 团队开会「综合整理访谈信息」，受访的是预约研究涉及的两个场点的志愿者。

examples.en: We decided to synthesise interviews before comparing staff accounts with the weekly booking figures.
examples.zh: 我们决定先「综合整理访谈信息」，再把员工的说法和每周预约数据作对照。

words.zhGloss: 访谈中反复出现的主题
words.enDefinition: Topics or patterns that emerge from what people say across a set of interviews.
acceptedZhAnswers: 访谈中反复出现的主题

examples.en: The main interview themes were unclear instructions and a lack of reminders for evening appointments.
examples.zh: 「访谈中反复出现的主题」主要是指引不清楚，以及晚间预约缺少提醒。

examples.en: We shared the interview themes with our adviser before choosing which examples to include.
examples.zh: 选定要写进去的例子之前，我们把「访谈中反复出现的主题」发给了指导老师。

words.enDefinition: The view of people who deal directly with customers, service users, or daily operations.

examples.en: The frontline perspective helped us see why the old form was still useful at busy times.
examples.zh: 「一线人员的视角」帮我们理解，为什么旧表格在繁忙时段还有用。

examples.en: We interviewed volunteer receptionists to include a frontline perspective in the museum's booking project.
examples.zh: 我们访谈了前台志愿者，把「一线人员的视角」纳入博物馆预约项目。

words.enDefinition: To compare what interviewees said with other accounts or records to see whether they agree.

examples.en: We took time to cross-check interview accounts before describing how each site recorded late collections.
examples.zh: 说明各场点怎样记录迟领之前，我们专门「交叉核对了访谈说法」。

examples.en: Our adviser asked us to cross-check interview accounts with the dates in the volunteer log.
examples.zh: 指导老师请我们结合志愿者日志里的日期「交叉核对访谈说法」。

collocations: cross-check interview accounts before drawing conclusions

words.enDefinition: To check that an observation or conclusion is supported by reliable information or further testing.

examples.en: We tried to validate a finding about late arrivals by checking the museum's group booking records.
examples.zh: 我们核对博物馆的团体预约记录，试着「核实一项发现」，它和迟到有关。

examples.en: The students returned on Saturday to validate a finding from their weekday observation of the queue.
examples.zh: 学生们周六再次到访，去「核实他们在工作日观察排队时的一项发现」。

collocations: validate a finding with additional data

words.enDefinition: A measurement taken before a change so later measurements can be compared with it.

examples.en: We used the average reply time as a baseline measure before the help desk changed its form.
examples.zh: 服务台换表格之前，我们用平均回复时间作为一个「基线指标」。

examples.en: The client asked which baseline measure we would compare with results from the reminder trial.
examples.zh: 客户问，我们会拿哪个「基线指标」来对比提醒试验的结果。

collocations: compare results with a baseline measure

words.enDefinition: To record how something works or performs before making a change so later results have a reference.

examples.en: We used the last month's attendance totals to establish a baseline before testing the reminder text.
examples.zh: 我们用上月到场总人数「建立比较基线」，再测试提醒文案。

examples.en: The team needed to establish a baseline for wait times before suggesting any changes to reception.
examples.zh: 团队需要先为等待时间「建立比较基线」，再对接待流程提出调整建议。

collocations: establish a baseline before the trial
use existing data to establish a baseline
help the client establish a baseline

words.enDefinition: A review of how a process, service, or organisation works before any proposed change is made.

examples.en: Our current-state assessment showed how the same request passed through three different desks at the theatre.
examples.zh: 「现状评估」显示，同一项申请在剧院内要经过三个不同的服务台。

examples.en: The current-state assessment included interviews and a review of one month's group booking records.
examples.zh: 「现状评估」包括访谈，以及查阅一个月的团体预约记录。

words.enDefinition: The way work is performed at present, including differences between written steps and actual practice.

examples.en: Our diagram showed the as-is process for booking a repair at the community bicycle workshop.
examples.zh: 这张图展示了社区自行车维修工场的「现行流程」，说明怎样预约维修。

examples.en: The volunteers checked whether the as-is process matched what they did on busy Saturdays.
examples.zh: 志愿者核对了「现行流程」，看看是否符合他们周六忙起来时的实际做法。

collocations: compare findings with the as-is process

words.enDefinition: A proposed sequence of activities showing how work would be done after changes are made.

examples.en: The future-state workflow showed how one shared form could replace the two separate booking lists.
examples.zh: 「拟议的新工作流程」展示了怎样用一张共用表格替代两份独立预约名单。

examples.en: The theatre staff reviewed our future-state workflow to see who would send the new reminders.
examples.zh: 剧院工作人员审查了「拟议的新工作流程」，看看由谁发送新的提醒。

words.zhGloss: 流程中让人受阻的环节
words.enDefinition: A part of a process that regularly causes frustration, delay, or extra work for people.
acceptedZhAnswers: 流程中让人受阻的环节

examples.en: We identified a process pain point where people had to repeat their requests to two desks.
examples.zh: 我们找到了「流程中让人受阻的环节」，人们得把同一个请求对两个服务台说两遍。

examples.en: The charity confirmed that missing names at collection were a process pain point for volunteers.
examples.zh: 慈善机构确认，领物名单漏人是志愿者「在流程中感到受阻的环节」。

words.enDefinition: A repeated return to an earlier step because work has to be corrected or done again.

examples.en: We found a rework loop when incomplete booking forms were returned to the desk each afternoon.
examples.zh: 每天下午总有没填全的预约表被退回服务台，我们发现了一个「反复返工的循环」。

examples.en: The client marked a rework loop where staff had to correct the same record repeatedly.
examples.zh: 客户标出一个「反复返工的循环」，员工得一再更正同一条记录。

collocations: find the cause of a rework loop

words.enDefinition: Information or responsibility that goes missing when work is passed between people, teams, or steps.

examples.en: The staff described a handoff gap between confirming a booking and preparing the workshop room.
examples.zh: 员工指出，从确认预约到布置工作坊房间，中间存在一个「交接环节的缺口」。

examples.en: We checked the two logs to find the handoff gap that left visitors without confirmations.
examples.zh: 我们核对了两份日志，查找导致访客没收到确认的「交接环节的缺口」。

words.enDefinition: Entering the same information more than once, or an extra record created in that way.

examples.en: We found a duplicate entry when the museum recorded one school group under two booking dates.
examples.zh: 博物馆把同一个学校团体登记在两个预约日期下，我们发现了这条「重复录入」的记录。

examples.en: The new form reduced duplicate entry by letting both desks refer to the same record.
examples.zh: 新表格让两个服务台共用同一条记录，减少了「重复录入」。

words.enDefinition: A manual task that lets people get work done despite a problem with the usual process.

examples.en: The repair shop used a manual workaround when the order form could not track borrowed tools.
examples.zh: 订单表无法跟踪借出的工具时，维修店用了「手动替代办法」。

examples.en: We documented the manual workaround because new volunteers were copying the same list every morning.
examples.zh: 新志愿者每天早晨都要抄一遍相同的名单，我们记录了这个「手动替代办法」。

words.enDefinition: A difference in how the same activity is performed in different cases, shifts, or locations.

examples.en: We found process variation when one branch took deposits and another branch only recorded names.
examples.zh: 一个分点收押金，另一个只登记姓名，我们发现了「流程做法的差异」。

examples.en: The team looked for process variation before interpreting the totals from different days of the week.
examples.zh: 团队先检查是否存在「流程做法的差异」，再解读一周里不同日期的汇总数据。

words.enDefinition: An observation supported by evidence from an investigation into how or why a problem occurs.

examples.en: The report listed a diagnostic finding about replies that staff drafted without ever sending them.
examples.zh: 报告列出一项「问题诊断所得的发现」，有些回复工作人员写了却一直没发。

examples.en: We shared a diagnostic finding about room changes before recommending a new reminder process.
examples.zh: 建议更改提醒流程前，我们分享了一项关于换房间的「问题诊断所得的发现」。

words.enDefinition: A record that lets someone trace an observation or claim back to its supporting material.

examples.en: We kept an evidence trail so the client could trace each queue estimate to its source.
examples.zh: 我们保留了「可追溯的证据记录」，这样客户能查到每项排队估算的来源。

examples.en: The adviser checked our evidence trail before asking how many bookings we had excluded.
examples.zh: 指导老师查阅了「可追溯的证据记录」，再问我们排除了多少项预约。

collocations: check the evidence trail for a finding

words.enDefinition: Missing information that limits what can be analysed or concluded from existing records.

examples.en: A data gap made it difficult to compare bookings confirmed before and after the holiday.
examples.zh: 有一处「数据缺口」，因此很难对比假期前后确认的预约。

examples.en: We mentioned the data gap upfront because the museum had no figures for weekend school visits.
examples.zh: 博物馆没有周末学校团体来访的数据，所以我们一开始就指出了「数据缺口」。

words.enDefinition: To ask someone to provide data that is needed but not included in what they already shared.

examples.en: We chose to request missing data for December before drawing conclusions about the winter bookings.
examples.zh: 我们决定先「索取缺失的十二月数据」，再对冬季预约下结论。

examples.en: The student team asked which office to contact to request missing data about group visits.
examples.zh: 学生团队问，应该联系哪个办公室来「索取缺失的数据」，这些数据和团体来访有关。

collocations: request missing data from a client
request missing data for a period
decide whether to request missing data

words.zhGloss: 检查是否存在抽样偏差
words.enDefinition: To look for ways in which a sample may systematically differ from the group it is intended to represent.
acceptedZhAnswers: 检查是否存在抽样偏差

examples.en: We needed to check for sampling bias because all the volunteers we interviewed worked on weekdays.
examples.zh: 我们采访的志愿者都在工作日值班，所以得「检查是否存在抽样偏差」。

examples.en: The adviser asked us to check for sampling bias before summarising the museum visitors' responses.
examples.zh: 指导老师请我们先「检查是否存在抽样偏差」，再总结博物馆访客的答复。

collocations: check for sampling bias in the responses
take time to check for sampling bias
check for sampling bias before interpreting results

words.enDefinition: A planned point at which the team checks its progress before continuing with more work.

examples.en: Our progress checkpoint came after the site visits and before we started testing new ideas.
examples.zh: 我们的「进度检查节点」安排在现场走访后、开始测试新想法前。

examples.en: We used a progress checkpoint to check whether the museum had provided all the booking totals.
examples.zh: 我们利用一次「进度检查节点」，确认博物馆是否提供了全部预约汇总数据。

collocations: review work at a progress checkpoint

words.enDefinition: A review around the middle of a project to discuss progress, early findings, and remaining work.

examples.en: The midpoint review helped us decide which problems deserved more attention before the next site visit.
examples.zh: 「中期项目评审」帮我们确定，下次实地走访前哪些问题值得进一步关注。

examples.en: Our client asked to invite the volunteer coordinator to the midpoint review on Friday.
examples.zh: 客户提出邀请志愿者协调员参加周五的「中期项目评审」。

collocations: discuss findings at a midpoint review

words.enDefinition: A presentation near the middle of a project sharing what the team has learned so far.

examples.en: The midpoint presentation included staff feedback on the theatre's two ways of confirming rehearsal bookings.
examples.zh: 「中期项目汇报」包括员工对剧院两种排练预约确认方式的反馈。

examples.en: We gave a midpoint presentation to show where museum visitors were getting stuck when booking.
examples.zh: 我们做了「中期项目汇报」，说明博物馆访客在预约时卡在哪一步。

collocations: include a finding in the midpoint presentation

words.enDefinition: Early findings that are becoming clear as an investigation continues.

examples.en: Our emerging findings suggested that the hardest step was finding a free room after school.
examples.zh: 我们「逐渐显现的调查结果」表明，最难的是放学后找到一间空房。

examples.en: The client asked about emerging findings after we finished visiting its second collection site.
examples.zh: 我们走访完第二个领取点之后，客户问起「逐渐显现的调查结果」。

collocations: share emerging findings with the client

words.enDefinition: Early suggestions for action that may change after more work or feedback.

examples.en: We shared preliminary recommendations about the reminder process while volunteers were still testing the wording.
examples.zh: 志愿者还在试用提示语时，我们分享了关于提醒流程的「初步建议」。

examples.en: The theatre manager reviewed our preliminary recommendations before we estimated the effort each would require.
examples.zh: 剧院经理先看了我们的「初步建议」，我们随后估算每条建议需要多少投入。

words.enDefinition: A conclusion based on information available so far that may change with more evidence.

examples.en: Our provisional conclusion changed when the cooperatives showed us how they counted rejected donations.
examples.zh: 几家合作社说明怎样统计未接收的捐赠物品后，我们的「暂定结论」改变了。

examples.en: We described the result as a provisional conclusion because only one site had been visited.
examples.zh: 因为只走访了一个场点，我们把这个结果写成「暂定结论」。

words.zhGloss: 检查调查发现是否合理
words.enDefinition: To see whether findings seem reasonable given the wider context or what people already know.
acceptedZhAnswers: 检查调查发现是否合理

examples.en: We asked staff to sense-check the findings before showing them to the cooperative's volunteer committee.
examples.zh: 把结果给合作社志愿者委员会看之前，我们请工作人员「检查调查发现是否合理」。

examples.en: The adviser offered to sense-check the findings against what the team had seen at both entrances.
examples.zh: 指导老师提出结合团队在两个入口看到的情况，「检查调查发现是否合理」。

collocations: sense-check the findings before sharing them

words.zhGloss: 请利益相关方参与测试
words.enDefinition: To try an idea, process, or design with people who will be affected and listen to their responses.
acceptedZhAnswers: 请利益相关方参与测试

examples.en: We needed something simple to test with stakeholders before changing the cooperative's entire collection process.
examples.zh: 更改合作社的整个领取流程之前，我们需要一个简单方案来「请利益相关方参与测试」。

examples.en: Our team drafted a reminder card to test with stakeholders who ran evening theatre sessions.
examples.zh: 团队草拟了提醒卡，打算「请负责晚间剧院活动的相关人员参与测试」。

collocations: choose what to test with stakeholders
prepare a draft to test with stakeholders
decide when to test with stakeholders

words.enDefinition: To explain something to the client in order, pointing out the key parts as you go.

examples.en: We used a diagram to walk the client through the way staff verified group bookings.
examples.zh: 我们用一张图「向客户逐步讲解」员工怎么核实团体预约。

examples.en: The students offered to walk the client through their figures before sharing the full report.
examples.zh: 学生们提出在分享整份报告前，先「逐步向客户讲解」这些数字。

collocations: walk the client through the draft
walk the client through the model
walk the client through each step

words.enDefinition: To check that the proposed steps are practical and achieve the intended result in relevant cases.

examples.en: We used a recent booking to validate the proposed workflow before asking volunteers to try it.
examples.zh: 请志愿者试用之前，我们用近期一笔预约「验证了拟议的工作流程」。

examples.en: The client helped us validate the proposed workflow using a request that involved two rehearsal rooms.
examples.zh: 客户帮我们用一项涉及两间排练室的申请「验证拟议的工作流程」。

collocations: use examples to validate the proposed workflow
validate the proposed workflow with staff
ask someone to validate the proposed workflow

words.enDefinition: A discussion or assessment of proposed actions before the client decides which to take forward.

examples.en: The client scheduled a recommendation review with staff who would have to change their booking routine.
examples.zh: 客户安排了「建议评审」，请需要更改预约日常流程的员工参加。

examples.en: We brought examples of both changes to the recommendation review so the museum could compare them.
examples.zh: 我们把两种改动的实例都带到「建议评审」上，让博物馆加以比较。

collocations: discuss priorities at the recommendation review

words.enDefinition: A meeting in which team members put evidence or ideas together to form a shared understanding.

examples.en: Our synthesis session combined queue observations with notes from the volunteer interviews we had completed.
examples.zh: 我们开了次「综合整理讨论会」，把排队观察情况和已完成的志愿者访谈记录合在一起分析。

examples.en: We booked a synthesis session after the last branch sent its figures for the semester.
examples.zh: 最后一个分点发来本学期的数据后，我们安排了「综合整理讨论会」。

collocations: bring evidence to a synthesis session

words.enDefinition: A repeating process in which people make a change, gather responses, and improve it again.

examples.en: The team built a feedback loop so staff could report problems after each reminder test.
examples.zh: 团队建立了「反馈循环」，让员工每次测试提醒后都能反映问题。

examples.en: A short feedback loop helped us correct the directions before the second set of visitors arrived.
examples.zh: 在第二批访客来之前，一个简短的「反馈循环」帮我们纠正了指引。

collocations: use a feedback loop to improve a process

words.enDefinition: One scheduled period or cycle in which the client reviews work and sends comments.

examples.en: We scheduled a client feedback round after the first draft of our museum booking report.
examples.zh: 博物馆预约报告出第一稿后，我们安排了「一轮客户反馈」。

examples.en: The client feedback round raised a question about how the group counted late repair collections.
examples.zh: 「这一轮客户反馈」提出了一个问题，是关于我们小组怎样统计延迟领取维修品。

collocations: include a client feedback round in the project

words.zhGloss: 与指导老师的进度沟通
words.enDefinition: A brief meeting with a faculty adviser to discuss how the student project is going.
acceptedZhAnswers: 与指导老师的进度沟通

examples.en: We raised the missing weekend records at our faculty check-in before choosing a different comparison.
examples.zh: 我们在「与指导老师的进度沟通」中提到周末记录缺失，之后选了另一种比较方法。

examples.en: Our faculty check-in covered the client meeting and which findings were ready to share.
examples.zh: 「与指导老师的进度沟通」谈到了客户会议，以及哪些发现已经可以分享。

collocations: raise a concern at the faculty check-in

words.enDefinition: To make clear what categories, terms, or measurements mean in the records used for analysis.

examples.en: We asked staff to clarify the data definitions for a repeat visitor before comparing the totals.
examples.zh: 比对汇总数据前，我们请员工「明确再次来访者的数据口径」。

examples.en: Our team needed to clarify the data definitions because two branches counted collections in different ways.
examples.zh: 两个分点统计取件次数的方式不同，我们团队需要「明确数据口径」。

collocations: clarify the data definitions with staff
take time to clarify the data definitions
clarify the data definitions before reporting

words.enDefinition: Questions or issues that still need discussion, information, or a decision.

examples.en: We listed open points from the meeting before asking the client who could answer them.
examples.zh: 我们列出了会议中「尚未解决的事项」，再问客户谁能回答。

examples.en: The project coordinator noted the open points so everyone knew what to check before Friday.
examples.zh: 项目协调员记下了「尚未解决的事项」，让大家知道周五前还要查什么。

words.enDefinition: To ask the client for information or views to help the team decide what to do.

examples.en: We paused to seek client input before deciding which branch should test the new volunteer form.
examples.zh: 我们先停下来「征求客户意见」，再决定由哪个分点试用新的志愿者表格。

examples.en: The student team agreed to seek client input on what should be included in the workshop.
examples.zh: 学生团队商定「征求客户意见」，了解工作坊应该包括哪些内容。

collocations: seek client input on the options
take time to seek client input

words.enDefinition: To write down the reasons why a particular project choice was made.

examples.en: Our note taker tried to capture decision rationale while the client explained its choice of site.
examples.zh: 客户说明为什么选这个场点时，记录员尽量「记录作出决定的理由」。

examples.en: We use the meeting summary to capture decision rationale so new members can understand earlier choices.
examples.zh: 我们用会议小结「记录作出决定的理由」，让新成员能理解此前的选择。

collocations: make sure to capture decision rationale
capture decision rationale after the meeting
capture decision rationale in the minutes

words.enDefinition: A record of the assumptions a project relies on and any updates when they are checked.

examples.en: We updated the assumptions log when the second branch explained how it counted repeat visitors.
examples.zh: 第二个分点解释怎样统计再次来访的访客后，我们更新了「假设记录表」。

examples.en: The assumptions log showed which ideas still needed to be checked against the booking data.
examples.zh: 「假设记录表」显示了哪些想法仍须用预约数据加以核实。

words.enDefinition: A record listing project risks and often how the team plans to monitor or handle them.

examples.en: The risk register listed possible delays if neither branch could provide its records before Friday.
examples.zh: 「项目风险登记表」列出了若两个分点周五前都无法提供记录，可能出现的延误。

examples.en: We checked the risk register before discussing which parts of the project might run late.
examples.zh: 讨论项目哪些部分可能延误之前，我们先看了「项目风险登记表」。

collocations: add an item to the risk register

words.enDefinition: To bring a possible problem that could affect the project to the team's or client's attention.

examples.en: I decided to raise a project risk when the museum rescheduled our only volunteer interview.
examples.zh: 博物馆改了唯一一场志愿者访谈的时间，我决定「提出一项项目风险」。

examples.en: Our team had to raise a project risk after learning the records were stored on paper.
examples.zh: 得知记录只存在纸上之后，我们团队不得不「提出一项项目风险」。

collocations: raise a project risk at a review
raise a project risk with the client

words.enDefinition: To return to the planned timetable after a delay or interruption.

examples.en: We shortened two interviews to get back on schedule after the museum closed early on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 博物馆周二提前关门后，我们缩短了两场访谈，好「赶上原计划」。

examples.en: The team could get back on schedule once the client gave us the missing figures.
examples.zh: 客户给了缺失的数据后，团队就可以「恢复按计划推进」。

collocations: help the team get back on schedule
try to get back on schedule
work together to get back on schedule

words.enDefinition: A plan for reducing the chance or likely effect of problems that could affect a project.

examples.en: Our risk mitigation plan identified another site to visit if the repair workshop had to close.
examples.zh: 我们的「降低项目风险的计划」列出了另一个可走访的场点，以防维修工场不得不关闭。

examples.en: We reviewed the risk mitigation plan when our main contact took a week off suddenly.
examples.zh: 主要联系人突然请了一周假，我们重新查看了「降低项目风险的计划」。

words.expression: check whether the issue is widespread
words.lemma: check whether the issue is widespread
words.enDefinition: To find out whether a problem occurs in many relevant places or situations.
acceptedEnVariants: check whether the issue is widespread

examples.en: We visited a second branch to check whether the issue is widespread across the charity.
examples.zh: 我们走访了第二个分点，「核查问题在这家慈善机构是否普遍」。

examples.en: The student team agreed to check whether the issue is widespread before recommending a process change.
examples.zh: 学生团队商定先「核查问题是否普遍」，再建议更改流程。

collocations: check whether the issue is widespread across sites
check whether the issue is widespread before responding
ask someone to check whether the issue is widespread

words.enDefinition: To make or check that the work addresses what the client considers most important.

examples.en: We reordered the recommendations to align with client priorities before sharing our first draft.
examples.zh: 分享第一稿前，我们调整了建议的顺序，使其「契合客户的优先事项」。

examples.en: Our adviser asked whether both options would align with client priorities for the next semester.
examples.zh: 指导老师问，两种方案是否都「契合客户下学期的优先事项」。

collocations: make sure recommendations align with client priorities
check whether findings align with client priorities
adapt the work to align with client priorities

words.enDefinition: To use the client's comments to revise or improve what the project team has prepared.

examples.en: We took a day to incorporate client feedback before sending the museum our updated recommendations.
examples.zh: 把更新的建议发给博物馆之前，我们花一天时间「把客户反馈纳入修改」。

examples.en: The students amended the diagram to incorporate client feedback about who confirmed the weekend bookings.
examples.zh: 学生们调整了图表，「把客户关于谁确认周末预约的反馈纳入修改」。

collocations: incorporate client feedback into the report
take time to incorporate client feedback
revise the draft to incorporate client feedback

words.zhGloss: 与客户共同开展的工作会
words.enDefinition: A meeting in which the client and project team work together on a particular problem or draft.
acceptedZhAnswers: 与客户共同开展的工作会

examples.en: We used a client working session to lay out the volunteer intake steps on cards.
examples.zh: 我们在「与客户共同开展的工作会」上，把招募志愿者的各个步骤写到卡片上排开。

examples.en: Both branches joined a client working session to rewrite the reminder text together on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 两个分点都参加了周二「与客户共同开展的工作会」，一起改写提醒文案。

collocations: bring a draft to the client working session

words.enDefinition: To record views that differ from the main view or proposed conclusion of the group.

examples.en: Our note taker made sure to capture dissenting views about the volunteer training schedule.
examples.zh: 记录员确保把关于志愿者培训安排的「不同意见记录下来」。

examples.en: We wanted to capture dissenting views before reporting which proposed changes the museum staff supported.
examples.zh: 汇报博物馆员工支持哪些拟议改动之前，我们想先「记录不同意见」。

collocations: capture dissenting views in the notes
make sure to capture dissenting views
capture dissenting views during a review

words.enDefinition: The parts of a draft or recommendation that should be improved first.

examples.en: Our revision priorities included clearer diagrams and fewer technical terms in the report for volunteers.
examples.zh: 我们的「优先修改的事项」包括把图画清楚，以及减少志愿者版报告里的术语。

examples.en: The client confirmed the revision priorities after reading comments from both teams at the theatre.
examples.zh: 客户看了剧院两个团队的意见后，确认了「优先修改的事项」。

collocations: confirm revision priorities with the client

words.enDefinition: To set an issue aside for later so the current discussion or work can continue.

examples.en: We agreed to park an issue about summer opening hours until the manager could join.
examples.zh: 我们商定先「暂时搁置一个问题」，就是夏季开放时间，等经理能参加再谈。

examples.en: The team decided to park an issue raised by the second branch until the data arrived.
examples.zh: 团队决定，数据到之前先「暂时搁置第二个分点提出的问题」。

collocations: decide to park an issue until the review
park an issue for later discussion

words.enDefinition: A presentation at the end of a project where the team shares its findings and recommendations with the client.

examples.en: Our final client presentation explained why the museum's weekend visitors needed different reminders from school groups.
examples.zh: 我们的「面向客户的最终汇报」解释了，为什么博物馆周末访客需要的提醒和学校团体不同。

examples.en: The student team rehearsed the final client presentation before showing the theatre director both booking alternatives.
examples.zh: 学生团队先排练了「面向客户的最终汇报」，再给剧院负责人看两种预约替代方案。

words.enDefinition: A written account of the consulting team's question, methods, findings, and recommendations for the client.

examples.en: The consulting report identified two ways the repair charity could track uncollected bicycles more consistently.
examples.zh: 「咨询报告」指出，维修慈善机构有两种方法可以更稳定地跟踪尚未被领走的自行车。

examples.en: We gave the client the consulting report and a short guide to reading the charts.
examples.zh: 我们给客户提供了「咨询报告」，还附上一份图表阅读简要指南。

words.zhGloss: 面向管理层的简明成果汇报
words.enDefinition: A short summary of findings or progress prepared for senior leaders who need to make decisions.
acceptedZhAnswers: 面向管理层的简明成果汇报

examples.en: The student team prepared an executive readout explaining the effect of the museum's current booking delays.
examples.zh: 学生团队准备了一份「面向管理层的简明成果汇报」，说明博物馆目前预约拖延带来的影响。

examples.en: The executive readout focused on the decision the charity's board needed to make that month.
examples.zh: 「面向管理层的简明成果汇报」聚焦慈善机构董事会当月需要作出的决定。

words.enDefinition: The reasons and evidence that explain why a particular course of action is recommended.

examples.en: Our recommendation rationale explained why one shared form would work better than two separate lists.
examples.zh: 我们写清了「提出建议的依据」，说明一张共用表比两份单独的名单更好用。

examples.en: The client asked for the recommendation rationale before presenting the proposal to its volunteer committee.
examples.zh: 在把方案提交给志愿者委员会之前，客户请我们提供「建议的依据」。

words.enDefinition: to designate the person who will coordinate implementation overall across the people and tasks involved

examples.en: The museum agreed to name an implementation lead before it tested the new group booking form.
examples.zh: 博物馆同意，在测试新的团体预约表前先「指定落实负责人」。

examples.en: We asked the charity to name an implementation lead to coordinate the work across both sites.
examples.zh: 我们请慈善机构「指定落实负责人」，协调两个场点的实施工作。

collocations: ask the client to name an implementation lead
agree to name an implementation lead
prepare to name an implementation lead

words.enDefinition: A plan describing the steps, timing, and responsibilities for putting a recommendation into practice.

examples.en: Our implementation plan assigned the theatre supervisor to check the first week's new booking records.
examples.zh: 我们的「实施计划」安排剧院主管核对头一周的新预约记录。

examples.en: The client wanted an implementation plan before asking two branches to change their confirmation messages.
examples.zh: 请两个分点更改确认消息之前，客户想先有一份「实施计划」。

words.enDefinition: An overview showing the main stages and order of work for carrying out a recommendation.

examples.en: The implementation roadmap showed a small trial before the form was introduced across both branches.
examples.zh: 「实施路线图」安排先小范围试用，再在两个分点都启用表格。

examples.en: We added a progress review between the two stages on the client's implementation roadmap.
examples.zh: 我们在客户的「实施路线图」上加了一次进度评审，放在两个阶段之间。

collocations: plot stages on an implementation roadmap

words.enDefinition: To try a proposed process with a small group or at one location before wider use.

examples.en: The repair charity decided to pilot the new process on Saturdays when more volunteers were present.
examples.zh: 维修慈善机构决定在志愿者较多的周六「小范围试行新流程」。

examples.en: We asked the museum to pilot the new process with one school group before wider use.
examples.zh: 我们请博物馆先找一个学校团体「小范围试行新流程」，再扩大使用范围。

collocations: choose where to pilot the new process
agree to pilot the new process
pilot the new process at one site

words.enDefinition: An assessment of a small trial to decide whether to continue, change, or stop what was tested.

examples.en: The pilot review showed that the new form saved time on weekday bookings at one site.
examples.zh: 「试行后的评审」显示，新表格节省了一个场点工作日的预约处理时间。

examples.en: We brought records from both weeks to the pilot review so the staff could compare them.
examples.zh: 我们把两周的记录都带到「试行后的评审」上，供员工比较。

collocations: discuss results at the pilot review

words.enDefinition: Things that make it difficult for people to start and continue using a new method or tool.

examples.en: One of the adoption barriers was that evening volunteers rarely checked the shared inbox.
examples.zh: 「采用新做法的障碍」之一，是晚间值班的志愿者很少查看共用收件箱。

examples.en: We discussed adoption barriers with staff before recommending that both sites use the same booking form.
examples.zh: 我们先和员工谈了「采用新做法的障碍」，才建议两个场点使用同一份预约表。

words.enDefinition: How ready an organisation is to introduce a change to all the people or locations involved.

examples.en: The client assessed rollout readiness after testing the instructions with two new volunteer groups.
examples.zh: 客户在两个新志愿者小组中测试了指引后，评估了「推广实施的准备程度」。

examples.en: Our team checked rollout readiness by asking which branches had already trained their reception staff.
examples.zh: 我们询问哪些分点已培训前台员工，以此检查「推广实施的准备程度」。

words.enDefinition: A practical guide that tells people how to do recurring work and handle common situations.

examples.en: The students wrote an operating playbook for handling bookings when two theatre rooms were requested together.
examples.zh: 学生们编写了「日常操作手册」，说明有人同时预约剧院的两个房间时该怎么处理。

examples.en: We added examples to the operating playbook so new volunteers could practise before their first shift.
examples.zh: 我们在「日常操作手册」中加了实例，让新志愿者首次值班前能练习。

collocations: use an operating playbook to train staff

words.enDefinition: Sharing the information and practical understanding needed for others to continue work after a project.

examples.en: We planned knowledge transfer so the charity could update its volunteer briefing without asking our team.
examples.zh: 我们规划了「知识移交」，让慈善机构以后自己就能更新志愿者工作说明。

examples.en: The last workshop focused on knowledge transfer to the people who would maintain the booking form.
examples.zh: 最后一次工作坊的重点，是向今后维护预约表的人做「知识移交」。

words.enDefinition: The transfer of a process, responsibilities, or materials to the team that will run them day to day.

examples.en: The handoff to operations included explaining who would update the repair queue at closing time.
examples.zh: 「移交给运营团队」时，我们解释了每天关门由谁更新维修队列。

examples.en: The museum asked us to include two short demonstrations in the handoff to operations next week.
examples.zh: 博物馆请我们在下周「移交给运营团队」时，安排两场简短演示。

collocations: prepare for the handoff to operations

words.zhGloss: 培养内部培训人员的活动
words.enDefinition: A session that prepares participants to teach a new process or skill to other people.
acceptedZhAnswers: 培养内部培训人员的活动

examples.en: The team ran a train-the-trainer session so supervisors could teach the new process to volunteers.
examples.zh: 团队举办了一次「培养内部培训人员的活动」，让主管能教志愿者使用新流程。

examples.en: At the train-the-trainer session, staff practised explaining what to do when a booking changed.
examples.zh: 在「培养内部培训人员的活动」中，员工练习讲解预约变更时该怎么做。

words.enDefinition: The final stage of a project when the team records remaining responsibilities and formally wraps up.

examples.en: During project closeout we checked that the museum had the editable files and the final report.
examples.zh: 「项目收尾」时，我们确认博物馆已经拿到了可编辑文件和最终报告。

examples.en: The client reviewed remaining actions at project closeout before introducing the permanent volunteer coordinator.
examples.zh: 在介绍今后长期负责的志愿者协调员之前，客户在「项目收尾」时查看了剩下要做的事。

words.enDefinition: A conversation with the client after a stage or project to review what happened and what to learn from it.

examples.en: Our client debrief covered which data took longest to collect and what helped us work together.
examples.zh: 「与客户的总结交流」谈到了哪些数据最难收集，以及哪些做法帮助了合作。

examples.en: The museum director used the client debrief to explain which recommendations her team would take forward.
examples.zh: 博物馆馆长在「与客户的总结交流」中说明，她的团队会落实哪些建议。

collocations: discuss lessons at the client debrief

words.enDefinition: Understanding gained from reflecting on what worked and what went wrong during a project.

examples.en: We wrote down lessons learned about doing site visits before asking volunteers to complete surveys.
examples.zh: 我们记下了「总结出的经验教训」，比如怎样在请志愿者做问卷前开展现场走访。

examples.en: The adviser shared our lessons learned with the next class before its first client meeting.
examples.zh: 指导老师在下一届学生首次见客户前，分享了我们「总结出的经验教训」。

collocations: apply lessons learned to another project

words.enDefinition: A later check on whether agreed changes have been put into practice and how they are working.

examples.en: We scheduled an implementation follow-up after the charity had used the appointment reminder for a month.
examples.zh: 慈善机构预约提醒用满一个月后，我们安排了「实施情况跟进」。

examples.en: The implementation follow-up helped the museum see why one site still used the earlier form.
examples.zh: 「实施情况跟进」帮博物馆知道了，为什么有一个场点仍用旧表格。

collocations: review results at an implementation follow-up

words.enDefinition: The change shown when current results are compared with the original measurement.

examples.en: We tracked progress against baseline by comparing the new reply times with the first week's results.
examples.zh: 我们把新的回复用时与第一周的结果相比，跟踪「相对于基线的进展」。

examples.en: The chart showed progress against baseline after the theatre staff adopted a single booking list.
examples.zh: 剧院员工改用一份预约名单后，图表展示了「相对于基线的进展」。

words.enDefinition: To count or estimate how many people have started using a new service, tool, or process.

examples.en: We used the booking totals to measure uptake after the gallery introduced the new request form.
examples.zh: 画廊启用新申请表后，我们用预约汇总数据来「衡量实际采用情况」。

examples.en: The repair charity planned to measure uptake without collecting any additional personal details from volunteers.
examples.zh: 维修慈善机构计划「衡量实际采用情况」，无需再收集志愿者的个人信息。

collocations: measure uptake of the new form

words.enDefinition: Information showing who started using a change and how it was used soon after introduction.

examples.en: The early adoption data showed more weekend volunteers used the booking form than we expected.
examples.zh: 「初期使用数据」显示，用预约表的周末志愿者比我们预计的多。

examples.en: We checked early adoption data before asking why one site kept using the old booking list.
examples.zh: 询问为什么有一个场点还在用旧预约名单前，我们看了「初期使用数据」。

collocations: share early adoption data with the team

words.zhGloss: 建议接下来采取的措施
words.enDefinition: Actions the project team advises the client to take after considering the findings.
acceptedZhAnswers: 建议接下来采取的措施

examples.en: Our recommended next steps included testing the clearer reminder language with two groups of visitors.
examples.zh: 我们「建议接下来采取的措施」包括，让两组访客试用更清楚的提醒用语。

examples.en: The client read the recommended next steps before asking which changes could start this term.
examples.zh: 客户看了「建议接下来采取的措施」后，问哪些调整本学期就可以开始。

words.enDefinition: A small set of recommendations kept for further consideration from a larger set of possibilities.

examples.en: We prepared a recommendation shortlist after the client ruled out moving to a new booking system.
examples.zh: 客户排除了更换预约系统的方案后，我们整理出一份「筛选后的建议清单」。

examples.en: The recommendation shortlist included a new reminder card and a simpler cancellation process.
examples.zh: 「筛选后的建议清单」包括改用新的提醒卡，以及简化取消预约的流程。

words.enDefinition: Recommendations ordered by importance, urgency, feasibility, or another agreed basis.

examples.en: Our prioritised recommendations put clearer visitor instructions ahead of redesigning the entire booking system.
examples.zh: 我们「按优先级排列的建议」把写清访客指引排在彻底重做预约系统之前。

examples.en: The director reviewed the prioritised recommendations and asked which one would help the volunteers first.
examples.zh: 负责人看了「按优先级排列的建议」，问哪一项能最快给志愿者带来帮助。

words.enDefinition: A useful improvement that can be achieved quickly and with relatively little effort.

examples.en: A clearer confirmation message was a quick win because the staff could update it immediately.
examples.zh: 写清楚确认消息是「短期就能见效的改进」，因为员工马上就能更新。

examples.en: We identified one quick win before discussing changes that would need a longer trial period.
examples.zh: 讨论需要较长时间试行的改动前，我们找出了一项「短期就能见效的改进」。

words.enDefinition: A recommendation intended to be carried out over a longer period or to have lasting effects.

examples.en: Our longer-term recommendation was to combine both sites' booking records after the museum replaced its software.
examples.zh: 我们「着眼长期的建议」是，博物馆换软件后把两处场点的预约记录合在一起。

examples.en: The team described weekly volunteer training as a longer-term recommendation because it needed sustained staffing.
examples.zh: 团队把每周志愿者培训列为「着眼长期的建议」，因为需要持续安排人手。

words.enDefinition: To add enough detail about what to do, who does it, and how, so someone can act on a recommendation.

examples.en: We added a suggested owner and timing to make the recommendation actionable for the charity.
examples.zh: 我们加上了建议负责人和时间安排，好让慈善机构的团队「实际执行这项建议」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to make the recommendation actionable by describing what staff would do first.
examples.zh: 老师请我们写清楚员工首先会做什么，「让建议可以实际执行」。

collocations: try to make the recommendation actionable
add steps to make the recommendation actionable
include a test to make the recommendation actionable

words.zhGloss: 单项改动的实施负责人
words.enDefinition: The person or team accountable for putting one agreed change or recommendation into practice.
acceptedZhAnswers: 单项改动的实施负责人

examples.en: The client named an implementation owner for each change when we handed over the project report.
examples.zh: 我们交付项目报告时，客户为每项改动都指定了「单项改动的实施负责人」。

examples.en: Our implementation owner checked whether both branches had added the revised reminder to their booking forms.
examples.zh: 我们的「单项改动的实施负责人」核对了两个分点有没有把新版提醒加进预约表。

words.enDefinition: To keep checking how a new process is being introduced and what happens during that period.

examples.en: The charity asked two supervisors to monitor the rollout and report where volunteers needed more help.
examples.zh: 慈善机构请两位主管「跟踪推广实施进度」，并报告哪些方面的志愿者还需要帮助。

examples.en: We gave the client a simple chart to monitor the rollout of its new reminder process.
examples.zh: 我们给了客户一张简单的图表，用来「跟踪新提醒流程的推广实施进度」。

collocations: ask someone to monitor the rollout
use a dashboard to monitor the rollout

words.enDefinition: To examine consequences of a change that the team did not originally intend or predict.

examples.en: The museum agreed to review unintended effects after one group had trouble with the new form.
examples.zh: 有个团体用新表格时遇到了麻烦，博物馆同意「检查非预期影响」。

examples.en: We asked the charity to review unintended effects before trying the new appointment process across branches.
examples.zh: 我们请慈善机构先「检查非预期影响」，再到各分点试用新的预约流程。

collocations: take time to review unintended effects
review unintended effects after a trial

words.enDefinition: To state what the project cannot establish because of limits in data, time, or methods.

examples.en: Our adviser asked us to report limitations because the data covered only the museum's busiest month.
examples.zh: 数据只涵盖博物馆最忙的一个月，指导老师请我们「说明分析的局限」。

examples.en: We chose to report limitations before discussing how the results might apply to other galleries.
examples.zh: 讨论结果能否用于其他画廊之前，我们先「说明分析的局限」。

collocations: report limitations in the final presentation
report limitations of a small sample
